methodologyNotes: Covers standalone guitar effects pedals (stompboxes) that a buyer researching pedalboard gear in 2026 would compare across distortion/fuzz/overdrive, modulation, reverb/delay, multi-effects, looper, and wah categories, sold at a published US price. Excludes rack units, amp-integrated effects, and software/plugin emulations. priceUsd is the manufacturer's current US MSRP where the manufacturer publishes one; where the manufacturer's own page could not be fetched (bot-blocked), priceUsd falls back to a named US retailer's listed price and priceNote says so explicitly. effect_type is a short free-text description of the pedal's primary function and notable sub-modes. true_bypass is true if the pedal routes the dry signal through a mechanical/relay true-bypass path when off, false if it uses a buffered/always-on signal path, or null if the manufacturer does not state this. power_draw_ma is the manufacturer-stated current draw in mA; where only a minimum power-supply requirement is published (not a measured draw), that minimum is used and the distinction is noted in the product's provenance. preset_count is the number of onboard preset/memory slots, or a short description when the scheme is tiered (e.g., onboard vs. MIDI-addressable); null for pedals with no preset storage (most analog stompboxes). stereo_io is true only if the pedal has both stereo inputs and stereo outputs. tap_tempo is true if a dedicated tap-tempo control (footswitch or MIDI CC) is documented; null if not mentioned in any fetched source, since silence does not confirm absence. midi_support is true if MIDI in/out/thru (5-pin DIN or TRS) is present. expression_input is true if the pedal has a dedicated jack for an external expression pedal or aux switch (built-in touch/pressure-sensitive footswitches like TC Electronic's MASH do not count, since they are not an external expression input). dimensions_in is the enclosure footprint as published, formatted 'W x D x H' in inches (converted from mm/cm where the source only gave metric); null where no fetched source stated dimensions.

Thomann's US listing corroborates the same model with matching mm dimensions (171 x 127 x 47mm ≈ 6.7 x 5.0 x 1.9in, consistent with Strymon's rounded imperial figures), the 500mA current draw, switchable true/buffered bypass, MIDI, and stereo I/O, and additionally dates the pedal to May 2024. Weight and a dedicated tap-tempo control are not stated on either fetched page, so both are left null/omitted. Image manually verified to depict this exact pedal (blue chassis, "BigSky MX" branding, three footswitches).

products.name: BOSS DS-1 Distortion
products.priceNote: BOSS does not publish a US MSRP on its own DS-1 spec page. West Music, a US retailer, lists "$69.99", consistent with widely-advertised US street pricing for this pedal.
products.provenance: BOSS's official DS-1 spec page confirms "10 mA" current draw, dimensions "73 mm (2-7/8 in) W x 129 mm (5-1/8 in) D x 59 mm (2-3/8 in) H", a 1978 introduction, mono in/out, no MIDI/expression/presets (fixed-control analog pedal), and 9V battery or optional adapter power. Wikipedia's DS-1 article corroborates the 1978 release and explicitly states the pedal uses buffered bypass, not true bypass: "the signal will pass through the input and output buffer stage of the effect, and this is the key differentiating factor between Boss pedals and 'true bypass' pedals." Weight and tap tempo are not applicable/stated. Image manually verified to depict this exact pedal (orange chassis, "Distortion DS-1" branding, Tone/Level/Dist knobs).
